$comment: Synthetic clinical corpus for TrialPulse local development, tests and evaluation. Entirely fabricated. Contains no real patient data and no confidential Meridian Therapeutics information. Facts listed here MUST appear in the generated document body verbatim so that the eval judges can assert on them.

study_context.indication: recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC)

sections.heading: 1. Study Design
facts: AXIOM-HN01 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study.
Planned enrollment is 480 participants across 92 sites.
Participants are randomized 1:1 to revarafusp alfa plus torilizumab or placebo plus torilizumab.

sections.heading: 2. Primary Endpoint
facts: The primary endpoint is overall survival (OS) in the PD-L1 CPS greater than or equal to 1 population.
The study is powered at 90% to detect a hazard ratio of 0.70.

sections.heading: 3. Key Inclusion Criteria
facts: Participants must be at least 18 years of age.
ECOG performance status must be 0 or 1.
Participants must have measurable disease per RECIST v1.1.

sections.heading: 4. Dose and Administration
facts: Revarafusp alfa is administered at 1500 mg intravenously every 3 weeks.
Torilizumab is administered at 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks.

sections.heading: 5. Interim Analysis
facts: A single interim analysis is planned after 60% of target OS events.
The interim analysis is reviewed by an independent Data Monitoring Committee.

sections.heading: 1. Study Design
facts: AXIOM-HN01 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study.
Planned enrollment is increased to 528 participants across 104 sites.
Participants are randomized 1:1 to revarafusp alfa plus torilizumab or placebo plus torilizumab.

sections.heading: 2. Primary Endpoint
facts: The primary endpoint is overall survival (OS) in the PD-L1 CPS greater than or equal to 1 population.
Progression-free survival was elevated from an exploratory endpoint to a key secondary endpoint in version 4.0.
The study is powered at 90% to detect a hazard ratio of 0.70.

sections.heading: 3. Key Inclusion Criteria
facts: Participants must be at least 18 years of age.
ECOG performance status must be 0 or 1.
Participants must have measurable disease per RECIST v1.1.
Version 4.0 permits enrollment of participants with treated, stable brain metastases.

sections.heading: 4. Dose and Administration
facts: Revarafusp alfa is administered at 1500 mg intravenously every 3 weeks.
Torilizumab is administered at 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks.
Version 4.0 adds a mandatory 60-minute observation period after the first infusion.

sections.heading: 5. Interim Analysis
facts: Version 4.0 adds a second interim analysis after 40% of target OS events.
The interim analysis is reviewed by an independent Data Monitoring Committee.

sections.heading: 6. Summary of Changes from Version 3.0
facts: Enrollment increased from 480 to 528 participants.
Site count increased from 92 to 104.
Brain metastases exclusion criterion was relaxed.
A second interim analysis was added.
A 60-minute post-infusion observation period was added.

sections.heading: 1. Study Design
facts: AXIOM-HN02 is an open-label Phase 2 study in first-line locally advanced HNSCC.
Planned enrollment is 120 participants across 28 sites.

sections.heading: 2. Primary Endpoint
facts: The primary endpoint of AXIOM-HN02 is objective response rate per RECIST v1.1.

sections.heading: 3. Dose and Administration
facts: Revarafusp alfa is administered at 1500 mg intravenously every 2 weeks in AXIOM-HN02.

sections.heading: 2. Mechanism of Action
facts: Revarafusp alfa is a bifunctional antibody targeting EGFR and TGF-beta.
The EGFR arm is a high-affinity IgG1 and the TGF-beta arm is a ligand trap.

sections.heading: 5. Reference Safety Information
facts: The expected adverse reactions include acneiform dermatitis, infusion-related reactions, and hypomagnesemia.
Edition 5 lists Grade 3 or higher acneiform dermatitis at an incidence of 11 percent.

sections.heading: 2. Mechanism of Action
facts: Revarafusp alfa is a bifunctional antibody targeting EGFR and TGF-beta.
The EGFR arm is a high-affinity IgG1 and the TGF-beta arm is a ligand trap.

sections.heading: 5. Reference Safety Information
facts: Edition 6 adds Grade 3 or higher hypertension as an identified risk.
Edition 6 revises Grade 3 or higher acneiform dermatitis incidence to 13 percent.
Infusion-related reactions remain an identified risk requiring premedication.

sections.heading: 7. Guidance for the Investigator
facts: Investigators must hold dosing for Grade 3 acneiform dermatitis until recovery to Grade 1 or lower.
Magnesium levels should be monitored every cycle.

sections.heading: 1. Summary of Clinical Progress
facts: As of 31 March 2026, impacted studies under IND 145678 have enrolled 412 participants cumulatively.
Two studies were active during the reporting period: AXIOM-HN01 and AXIOM-HN02.

sections.heading: 3. Changes in the Investigator Brochure
facts: Investigator Brochure Edition 6 was distributed to all active sites in May 2026.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose of Amendment
facts: Amendment 12 submits AXIOM-HN01 Protocol version 4.0 to the FDA.
Amendment 12 was submitted on 09 June 2026 and the 30-day review period ended on 09 July 2026.

sections.heading: 2. Pending Amendments
facts: Amendment 13 covering the updated statistical analysis plan is pending and targeted for submission in September 2026.
Amendment 14 covering the AXIOM-HN02 dose expansion cohort is pending internal review.

sections.heading: 1. Meeting Request
facts: Meridian requests a Type B pre-NDA meeting with the FDA Division of Oncology 2.
The pre-NDA meeting is scheduled for 12 November 2026.
The meeting package is due to the FDA 30 days in advance, on 13 October 2026.

sections.heading: 2. Questions for the Agency
facts: Question 1 asks whether the proposed OS analysis population is acceptable for registration.
Question 3 asks whether the immunogenicity assay validation package is sufficient.

documents.title: FDA Type B Meeting Minutes - End of Phase 2

sections.heading: 1. Attendees
facts: The meeting was held on 08 October 2025 with the FDA Division of Oncology 2.
The Meridian regulatory lead of record is Alina Ferreira.

sections.heading: 2. Agency Feedback
facts: The Agency agreed that overall survival is an acceptable primary endpoint.
The Agency recommended that progression-free survival be collected as a key secondary endpoint.

sections.heading: 2. Aggregate Adverse Events by System Organ Class
facts: Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders were reported in 218 events during Q2 2026.
Gastrointestinal disorders were reported in 141 events during Q2 2026.
Metabolism and nutrition disorders were reported in 96 events during Q2 2026.
Vascular disorders were reported in 47 events during Q2 2026.

sections.heading: 3. Serious Adverse Events
facts: There were 34 serious adverse events reported in Q2 2026.
Six serious adverse events were assessed as related to revarafusp alfa.
There were no treatment-related deaths in Q2 2026.

sections.heading: 4. Narrative Summaries
facts: Participant 014-0032, a 61-year-old male, experienced Grade 4 infusion-related reaction on Cycle 1 Day 1.
Participant 027-0011, initials J.M., experienced Grade 3 hypertension requiring dose interruption.

sections.heading: 3. Cumulative Exposure
facts: Cumulative exposure across the revarafusp alfa program is 1,284 participant-years as of 31 March 2026.

sections.heading: 6. Signal Evaluation
facts: Hypertension was evaluated as an emerging safety signal and added to the reference safety information.
No new signal was identified for hepatotoxicity during the reporting period.

sections.heading: 1. Line Listing
facts: Three SUSARs were reported in Q2 2026 and all were expedited to the FDA within 15 calendar days.
Participant 003-0007, date of birth 14 March 1958, experienced a Grade 4 pneumonitis SUSAR.

documents.title: Site US-014 Monitoring Visit Follow-up Letter

sections.heading: 1. Visit Summary
facts: An interim monitoring visit was conducted at site US-014 on 18 June 2026.
Source data verification was completed for 12 of 12 enrolled participants.

sections.heading: 2. Action Items
facts: Site US-014 must file the updated delegation of authority log within 10 business days.
Two informed consent forms at site US-014 require re-consent to Protocol version 4.0.

sections.heading: 1. Deviation Description
facts: Site US-027 reported a major protocol deviation on 27 May 2026 involving an out-of-window tumor assessment.
The tumor assessment was performed 11 days outside the protocol-specified window.

sections.heading: 2. Corrective and Preventive Action
facts: Site US-027 must retrain all study coordinators on visit windows by 30 June 2026.

sections.heading: 1. Protocol Version 4.0 Rollout
facts: Protocol version 4.0 became effective on 02 June 2026 and all sites must implement it after IRB approval.
Sites should submit Protocol version 4.0 to their IRB within 14 days of receipt.

sections.heading: 2. Enrollment Update
facts: Cumulative AXIOM-HN01 enrollment reached 366 participants as of 31 May 2026.

sections.heading: 1. Enrollment Status
facts: Site EU-003 has enrolled 4 participants against a target of 9 participants.
Site EU-003 is asked to submit a recruitment mitigation plan by 15 July 2026.

sections.heading: 1. Late-Stage Competitors
facts: Four bispecific programs are in Phase 3 development for first-line R/M HNSCC as of Q2 2026.
Torilizumab monotherapy remains the standard of care comparator in first-line PD-L1 positive disease.

sections.heading: 3. Readout Timing
facts: The nearest competitor Phase 3 overall survival readout is projected for the second half of 2027.

sections.heading: 1. Active Combination Studies
facts: Twenty-two active torilizumab combination studies in HNSCC were identified in June 2026.
Nine of those studies are sponsored by academic consortia.

sections.heading: 1. Program Overview
facts: The competing EGFR/LGR5 bispecific reported a 63 percent objective response rate in a Phase 2 first-line cohort.
The competing program initiated its Phase 3 study in March 2026.

sections.heading: 2. Payer Considerations
facts: US payers are expected to require PD-L1 CPS testing as a coverage condition for combination therapy.
The estimated annualized cost of care for first-line R/M HNSCC combination therapy is 214,000 US dollars.
